_instructions: Correction rule table for RQ3. Drafted by Hena from the cited troubleshooting guides and papers, without consulting src/independent_reference.py or docs/INDEPENDENT_REFERENCE_TABLE.md. Parameter names come from parameter_vocabulary; direction is INCREASE, DECREASE, ENABLE or CHECK.
author: Hena Parween (drafted for the team; review by Agya Aboagye-Otchere pending)

primary_action.delta: +0.5 to 1 mm (direct drive) or +1 to 2 mm (Bowden)

stringing.physical_rationale: Molten filament oozes from the nozzle during travel moves. More retraction relieves nozzle pressure, a cooler melt is more viscous and oozes less, and faster travel leaves less time to ooze.
citations: De La Rosa, Armani and Golmohamadi (2024), Defect Detection and Closed-loop Feedback Using Machine Learning for Fused Filament Fabrication, Procedia CIRP 126
Prusa Research Knowledge Base, print quality troubleshooting (help.prusa3d.com)

warping.physical_rationale: Upper layers cool and shrink while the first layer is held on the bed, so corners lift. A warmer bed keeps the base near the glass transition temperature, a brim adds contact area, and an enclosure reduces the temperature gradient.
citations: Prusa Research Knowledge Base, print quality troubleshooting (help.prusa3d.com)

primary_action.delta: tighten loose X/Y belts and pulley set screws

secondary_actions.delta: reduce jerk/acceleration or raise motor current if steps are skipped

layer_shifting.physical_rationale: Layers shift when the X or Y axis loses position: a loose belt or pulley slips, or the motor skips steps because the head moves faster than the motor torque allows.
citations: Prusa Research Knowledge Base, print quality troubleshooting (help.prusa3d.com)

under_extrusion.physical_rationale: Too little plastic leaves the nozzle for the commanded path. A higher flow multiplier asks for more material, a hotter nozzle lowers melt viscosity so the extruder can push it, and a slower speed lowers the required volumetric flow.
citations: De La Rosa, Armani and Golmohamadi (2024), Defect Detection and Closed-loop Feedback Using Machine Learning for Fused Filament Fabrication, Procedia CIRP 126
Jin, Zhang and Gu (2019), Autonomous in-situ correction of fused deposition modeling printers using computer vision and deep learning, Manufacturing Letters 22

over_extrusion.physical_rationale: More plastic is deposited than the path needs, giving blobs and rough walls. A lower flow multiplier removes the excess, and a cooler nozzle with more cooling makes the extra material sag and spread less.
citations: De La Rosa, Armani and Golmohamadi (2024), Defect Detection and Closed-loop Feedback Using Machine Learning for Fused Filament Fabrication, Procedia CIRP 126
Jin, Zhang and Gu (2019), Autonomous in-situ correction of fused deposition modeling printers using computer vision and deep learning, Manufacturing Letters 22

primary_action.delta: re-level the bed / run mesh bed levelling

bed_adhesion.physical_rationale: The first layer does not stick when the nozzle is too far from the bed or the gap varies across it. Levelling and a smaller nozzle gap press the first layer into the bed, and a slower first layer gives it time to bond.
citations: Prusa Research Knowledge Base, print quality troubleshooting (help.prusa3d.com)
